questions.q: How does Hoffman suggest you treat a “no” from an investor?
a: As a chance to reassess the idea and fix its weaknesses
As proof that the business idea cannot succeed
As a reason to stop pitching and work alone
As a signal to copy whatever the investor funds instead
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a no should not stop you but should help you reevaluate and strengthen your idea.

questions.q: How can you learn what customers really want?
a: Watch what they do rather than what they say
Survey them and follow the most popular answer
Copy the features of the market leader
Ask investors which products will sell best
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a great way to know customer thinking is to observe their actions, not their words.

questions.q: What did Airbnb do when the pandemic disrupted its core business?
a: It adapted by promoting remote work stays, virtual tours and local activities
It shut down all operations until travel returned to normal
It raised prices to make up for the lost bookings
It sold the company to a traditional hotel chain
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses Airbnb to show that great leaders improvise and adapt when their business model is threatened.

questions.q: What does the Starbucks example illustrate about leadership?
a: A company can prioritize social responsibility before becoming profitable
Great leaders should avoid spending money on employees
Health benefits are only worthwhile once a company is large
Profit must always come before any community commitment
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes Starbucks offered comprehensive health insurance to employees before it was profitable.

questions.q: What should you check before scaling through referrals or big promotions?
a: Whether your company can handle the sudden demand
Whether your competitors are running similar campaigns
Whether investors approve of the marketing budget
Whether customers will pay more after the promotion
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns that promotions can speed growth, but you must know whether you can handle the response.
